title: How Long Does a Solar Panel Take to Charge a Power Station? (100 W, 200 W, 400 W)
short_title: A 200 W solar panel doesn't give you 200 W
summary: How many hours of sun a 100 W, 200 W or 400 W folding panel takes to refill a 288 Wh, 1 kWh or 2 kWh power station, why a panel delivers only 60-75% of its rating, how many watt-hours a panel puts back in a day, and the station's solar input limit that caps it all.
short_summary: A folding solar panel delivers about 60-75% of its rating in good sun. Divide the battery's watt-hours by that to get the hours of sun a refill takes.
tags: how long to charge power station with solar panel

long.say: How long does a solar panel take to refill a portable power station? The answer on the box is almost always too optimistic. Here's the honest math for hundred, two-hundred and four-hundred-watt panels. Quick note: if you buy through the links in the description, Dealectric earns a commission, at no cost to you.

long.say: Start here: a folding panel delivers roughly sixty to seventy-five percent of its rating in good sun. Heat, the angle to the sun and the wiring all take a cut; Popular Mechanics measured fifty to seventy-five percent. So a hundred-watt panel gives you about seventy-five watts, not a hundred.

slide.cap: of its rating is what a folding panel delivers in good sun
slide.note: So a 100 W panel gives about 75 W

long.say: So the formula is simple. Hours of full sun equal the battery's watt-hours, divided by the panel's watts times about point seven. A one-thousand-twenty-four watt-hour battery with a two-hundred-watt panel: one thousand twenty-four, divided by about a hundred forty, is about seven to eight and a half hours.

items: Hours of full sun ≈ battery Wh ÷ (panel W × 0.6–0.75)
Example: 1,024 Wh with a 200 W panel

long.say: Here's the whole chart. A two-hundred-eighty-eight watt-hour station refills in four to five hours from a hundred-watt panel. A one-kilowatt-hour station needs seven to eight and a half hours from two hundred watts, or three and a half to four and a half from four hundred. A two-kilowatt-hour station needs fourteen to seventeen hours from two hundred watts, which is two or three sunny days.

slide.foot: At 60–75% of the panel's rating; from empty, in full sun

long.say: Most places get about four and a half peak-sun hours a day, averaged over the year. That makes a hundred-watt panel worth about three hundred forty watt-hours a day, and a two-hundred-watt panel about six hundred seventy-five. In winter or under cloud, plan on much less.

slide.note: 100 W panel ≈ 340 Wh a day · 200 W ≈ 675 Wh a day

long.say: Now the ceiling. Every station has a maximum solar input, in watts and in volts. BLUETTI's Elite 30 V2 takes two hundred watts at twelve to twenty-eight volts, so a big forty-volt folding panel won't work with it. The AC180 takes five hundred watts at twelve to sixty volts, and ALLPOWERS' P1800 takes six hundred fifty. More panel than the input allows just goes to waste, and too many volts can stop it charging.
